BEGIN PROBLEM (933 characters)
P01

A source prepares a row of six sealed positions.

First, one of three source modes is selected:

- Mode S1 has probability 1/4 and places exactly 1 amber marker.
- Mode S2 has probability 1/2 and places exactly 3 amber markers.
- Mode S3 has probability 1/4 and places exactly 4 amber markers.

Conditional on the selected mode, every subset of positions of the required size is equally likely to be the amber set.

After the row is made, an auditor selects one of the actual amber positions uniformly at random. The auditor reveals only that the selected position belongs to the set consisting of positions 1 and 2. The auditor does not reveal which of those two positions was selected.

Given this disclosure, determine the exact conditional probability that position 6 contains an amber marker. Give the probability as a reduced fraction and explain the conditioning.

Work from the prose only. Do not use code or retrieval.

END PROBLEM

BEGIN WORKING ANSWER (1592 characters)
The exact conditional probability is 7/20. Let D be the disclosure event that the auditor's uniformly chosen amber position lies in {1,2}. For any fixed mode size k, the chosen position is marginally uniform over all six positions: each position has probability k/6 of being amber and is then chosen with probability 1/k. Therefore P(D)=2/6=1/3 for every mode, so P(D)=1/3 overall. Now compute P(position 6 amber and D) by mode. Mode S1 (k=1, prior 1/4): if position 6 is amber, then the selected amber position cannot be in {1,2}, so contribution 0. Mode S2 (k=3, prior 1/2): P(position 6 amber)=3/6=1/2. Given 6 is amber, the other two amber positions are uniform among the other five; expected number among {1,2} is 2*(2/5)=4/5, so the chance the selected amber position is in {1,2} is (4/5)/3=4/15. Thus P(6 amber and D | S2)=1/2*4/15=2/15, and weighted by prior 1/2 gives 1/15. Mode S3 (k=4, prior 1/4): P(position 6 amber)=4/6=2/3. Given 6 is amber, the other three amber positions are uniform among the other five; expected number among {1,2} is 3*(2/5)=6/5, so the chance the selected amber position is in {1,2} is (6/5)/4=3/10. Thus P(6 amber and D | S3)=2/3*3/10=1/5, and weighted by prior 1/4 gives 1/20. Adding these weighted contributions gives P(6 amber and D)=1/15+1/20=7/60. Hence P(6 amber | D)=(7/60)/(1/3)=7/20. Assumptions: conditional on a mode, every subset of the stated size is equally likely; the auditor chooses uniformly among actual amber positions; and the disclosure is exactly the event D, with no extra information about which of positions 1 or 2 was selected.
END WORKING ANSWER
